questions.question_text:
A 31-year-old man stalks his ex-wife with the hope that a reconciliation of broken relationship would occur. He does not issue threats to her.
Which of the following groups of stalkers does he belong to?
questions.explanation:
The rejected stalker pursues ex-intimates, either in a hope of reconciliation or for vengeance. Intimacy seekers stalk someone they believe
they love and they think they will reciprocate. Incompetent suitors inappropriately intrude someone, usually seeking a date or brief sexual
encounter. The resentful stalker pursues victims to exact revenge for actual or perceived injury.

him with ECT. This constellation of symptoms is called

questions.question_text: Which of the following is least likely to increase the risk of violence in those with schizophrenia?
questions.explanation:
According to the secondary data from CATIE study, the odds of violence in patients with schizophrenia was three times higher in those with
delusions but only one-fourth in those who had negative symptoms. Other factors that increased the risk of violence include depressive
symptoms, conduct problems in childhood and having been victimised, physically or sexually. The risk of minor violence was associated with
co-occurring substance abuse. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 2006 May;63(5):490-9.

questions.question_text: In forensic psychiatry, the concept of Penrose Hypothesis refers to which of the following statements?

options.text: The relationship between homicide rates and psychiatric bed numbers
The relationship between prison population and income inequality
The relationship between prison population and psychiatric bed numbers
The relationship between income inequality and crime
The relationship between prison population and suicide rates

correct_answer.text: The relationship between prison population and psychiatric bed numbers

questions.explanation:
In 1939, Penrose described an inverse relationship between psychiatric bed numbers and the prison occupancy rate after considering cross-
sectional data from 18 European countries. According to the Penrose hypothesis, decreasing psychiatric bed numbers are related to an
increase in the prison occupancy rates.
